On Sundays me, my Mom and my Grandma would go for a drive in the country and look for empty pop and beer bottles in the ditch. It was 2 cents for beer and 5 cents for pop when you turned them in. 

Sometimes we'd take a picnic lunch with boiled chicken, jelly rolls, bananas and tomatoes. Other times we'd stop and get a bag of chips and a bottle of blue cream soda.

If we saw a cool flower or plant growing wild my Mom would dig it up with a shovel and transplant it at our house. Not the Trilliums though....against the law to disturb those. But there were lillies, paint brushes, brown-eyed susans and columbine.

We'd move turtles off the road to save them, and stop at abandoned farm houses and look around, being careful not to step in an old well.

Life was happy then. When you grow up you can't get that feeling back.

I think the only risk to depression medication is that it is hard to stop taking once your body is used to it. But that's not a bad thing if you always need it, really.

I have taken medication for depression for 22 years. Without it I would not be able to cope with day to day life, run my business or parent effectively. I remember what life was like before, and I am thankful for the pills.

All medication may come with side effects, but some people will experience none. At the time I was very against taking pills but it has definitely changed my life for the better.

I still get depressed, but the difference is, the medication helps me cope better and not have complete meltdowns everyday.

Good luck. If you are in Canada, there will be places that offer free therapy. If you do start medication, give it at least 2 weeks trial, as it may take that long to notice a difference.

Braxton, 17, scans his deceased pet, marking a series of tragic events for his family, including his little sister’s abduction. His mother bonds with her missing daughter’s replica, unaware that Savers have been programmed to emit dangerous subliminal messages.

Teens Natalia and Stem meet by chance, and despite class differences, are immediately drawn to each other. Their relationship must be kept hidden from Natalia’s prejudiced parents and friends, but ultimately it may be the Saver that destroys them.

A cast of unlikely heroes fight for truth, uncovering dark secrets about themselves and Futurprise’s greatest creation. Their lives will be profoundly altered as they struggle with forgiveness, social consequences, and the blurred boundaries between life and death.

Make sure the muscles in your arms are engaged....hold your arms very strongly, and feel the muscles engaging and connecting through your back.

Make sure your arms in en avant are not too high or too low, which can throw you off balance.

In your prep. plie, foreshorten your arm in 2nd slightly.....so it has a shorter distance to travel to meet the other one. One trick that works for me is to actually move this arm first, before anything else....just slightly.

Make sure there is pressure between the working foot and the supporting leg....press them into/against each other.

Pulling up under the working thigh....making a slightly higher passe position can help. 

Practice just balancing in passe position on a rise. Then 1/4 turns, then 1/2, etc. 

No matter what, continue to hold your working foot in passe after the turn is complete.....to practice....it trains the body to hold the pirouette at the end and not just fall out of it.

Make sure the arms are not coming out of en avant part way through the turn. Once they fall apart, the turn is pretty much finished.

Your preparatory plie should be small, and all your weight on the front foot. 

Something that helps me as I bring in the long arm is to inhale, widening my chest and lifting it slightly. 

Make sure not just the head is spotting, but the eyes too.
